title: K_{s,t} Generalization of C₄-Free Subgraphs
description: Generalizes Erdős 1008 from C₄-free to K_{s,t}-free subgraphs. Axiomatizes the Conlon-Fox-Sudakov result: every graph with m edges has a K_{s,t}-free subgraph with Ω(m^{1-1/s}) edges.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)
originalContributions: c4_from_kst: C4 case as K_{2,2} corollary (PROVED)
meta.assumptions: Two axioms: K_{s,t}-free subgraph existence (CFS 2014) and exponent optimality. Both require probabilistic method.

overview.historicalContext: The Zarankiewicz problem (1951) asks for the maximum number of edges in a bipartite graph avoiding $K_{s,t}$; the Kővári-Sós-Turán theorem (1954) gives the upper bound $O(n^{2-1/s})$. Erdős Problem 1008 asks about guaranteed $C_4$-free subgraphs in dense graphs. Conlon, Fox, and Sudakov (2014, arXiv:1401.6711) generalized this to all complete bipartite forbidden subgraphs, proving that every graph with $m$ edges has a $K_{s,t}$-free subgraph with $\Omega(m^{1-1/s})$ edges. Their proof combines random vertex sampling with the Kővári-Sós-Turán bound to control the expected number of forbidden copies. The exponent $1 - 1/s$ is tight by Zarankiewicz constructions.
overview.problemStatement: Does every graph with m edges contain a K_{s,t}-free subgraph with Ω(m^{1-1/s}) edges?
overview.text: Generalizes C₄-free subgraph existence to K_{s,t}-free.
overview.proofStrategy: Probabilistic method: random vertex sampling with Kővári-Sós-Turán control.
keyInsights: C₄ = K_{2,2} gives the parent result as special case
The CFS paper uses a degeneracy parameter for tighter bounds

sections.title: K_{s,t}-Freeness
sections.mathContext: IsKstFree(G, s, t): ¬∃ A B, |A|=s ∧ |B|=t ∧ A∩B=∅ ∧ ∀ a∈A, b∈B, G.Adj a b. For s=t=2 this is C₄-freeness.

sections.title: K_{s,t} Subgraph Theorem
sections.mathContext: CFS (2014): ∀ G with m edges, ∃ K_{s,t}-free H ⊆ G with |E(H)| ≥ c·m^{1-1/s}. Probabilistic deletion via random vertex sampling.

sections.title: C₄ Recovery
sections.summary: Recovers the C₄ case as K_{2,2} corollary.
sections.mathContext: C₄ = K_{2,2} gives exponent 1-1/2 = 1/2, weaker than parent's 2/3. The gap reflects CFS degeneracy refinement vs crude K_{s,t} bound.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the K_{s,t} generalization of Erdős 1008 with 2 axioms and 1 proved corollary.
conclusion.implications: Reveals the role of Kővári-Sós-Turán exponents in extremal subgraph problems.
openQuestions: Can the K_{s,t} result be extended to non-bipartite forbidden graphs?
Prove via probabilistic method when Mathlib gains random graph support
